title: The Wheel Stops
lead: Madame Oriel raises her voice. Nobody on the Gilded Wheel has ever heard it before, and it comes over every speaker on the station at once, and what she says is "Everyone will now walk, please, to the nearest dock." Beneath your feet the floor has begun, very slightly, to tilt.
anyone: Madame Oriel has raised her voice. Nobody on the Gilded Wheel has ever heard it before, and it comes over every speaker on the station at once, and what she says is "Everyone will now walk, please, to the nearest dock." The floor has begun, very slightly, to tilt.

gm.truth: Whatever the captain did about the mind in the walls, the Wheel has come to the end of what eighty years of patching can do. Without Quartile in full control, or with Quartile distracted, or simply because Quartile has had enough, the spin bearing that gravity depends on is failing, and the station is coming apart slowly. Twelve thousand gamblers, staff and indebted people are aboard, and there are boats for four thousand. The Wheel keeps its debtors down in the Cellars under lock, for their own safety, and the only person who can open those locks is Oriel. Oriel is standing at the master board, perfectly calm, and she won't leave. The twist: she's been expecting this for years and has quietly bought up every lifeboat contract in the sector. She has a plan. It saves the House's assets first, in order of value, and she has a printed list. It's a very good plan. If the captain tears up her list to save the debtors first, about a thousand more paying customers, some of them powerful and some of them innocent, won't make it to the boats in time. The fleet, close by, is the only thing with enough empty space, and it can't feed anyone who comes aboard.
beats: The tilt. Chips slide off the tables and roll, all together, toward one wall. Then the noise starts, and a very expensive crowd stops being polite.
The list. Oriel hands it over without being asked: who gets the boats, ranked by what they're worth. The captain's own name is near the top, along with an offer of a seat.

The Cellars: locked doors, debtors pounding very politely and then not politely, and a floor manager with a key and a contract and a terrible decision. Kit is already down there, for once in their life not running.
The bearing. Dunn Marrow on comms, swearing with something like reverence at how badly it's been maintained, says he can buy some time by doing a very stupid thing.
The last boat. Oriel at her board, and a choice about whether to leave her there. She offers a bet on whether the captain will come back for her.
routes: Hold the station together: engineering and void_ops on the bearing to buy an hour, with piloting to bring fleet shuttles into a spinning, tilting dock.
Move the crowd: leadership, tactics and intimidation to turn twelve thousand panicking people into lines, and open the Cellars.
Move the list: persuasion, commerce or hacking to change Oriel's order of rescue, or to make the people at the top of it give up their seats.
checks: engineering:very_hard to stabilize the spin bearing
piloting:hard to dock a shuttle with a tilting station
leadership:hard to turn a panicking crowd into a line
void_ops:hard to get out on the hull and set the braces
persuasion:very_hard to change Madame Oriel's mind about anything
athletics:moderate to cross a floor that's becoming a wall
fights: wheel_enforcer guarding the boats, and desperate_refugee who've stopped listening. A clear order, the right list or an open door takes the fight out of most of them.
outcomes: If the Cellars are opened first, thousands of debtors live, and they owe nothing, because the ledgers are gone. The fleet takes on far more people than it can feed, and powerful families across known space have new reasons to hate the captain.
If Oriel's list is followed, the House survives, its wealth is intact, and the fleet gets a huge payment and a very heavy silence from the survivors. Morale falls hard.
If the station is saved, by some miracle of Marrow's, the Gilded Wheel limps on, under new management or the same management. Nobody there can ever again look at the captain and see a mark.

If the captain goes back for Oriel, she keeps her word about any bet she's made, and her marker on the captain, if there's one, gets very much lighter. Her fate and whether she'll accept rescue are hers to decide in the moment.
gm.rewards: Whatever survivors press on the captain: a surgeon_lens, 500 credits, two refined_fuel from the station's stores. Fleet standing that swings hard, and an enormous, mixed reputation.
